intro: Today you lay the first stone. It's small, and that's perfect.
task: I do one small task
just one, that takes less than 5 minutes.
Do
ideas: make my bed · wash a mug · put away my shoes · open the window
fill: My small task today:
motto: Whether you ticked one box or all three, you showed up. That's day 1.
Tomorrow the shadow moves forward one step. So do you.

intro: Yesterday you started. Today you came back. That already is consistency.
task: I make my bed
even quickly, even imperfectly: just pulled up.
Make
ideas: sheets pulled up · pillow in place · blanket folded
fill: How it felt to see my bed made:
motto: The sun doesn't ask itself whether it feels like rising. It just rises.
Two days in a row: your shadow is starting to draw a path.

intro: A little air, a little light: sometimes that's all it takes to wake up the day.
task: I open the window and breathe
3 deep breaths, slowly, facing the daylight.
Breathe
ideas: breathe in through the nose · breathe out gently · look at the sky
fill: What I saw or felt through the window:
motto: A sundial needs light to work. So do you.
Three days: you're already in the middle of the week.

intro: No need to tidy everything. Just one thing put back in its place, and the space can breathe.
task: I tidy just one thing
one object, one corner, one surface. No more.
Tidy
ideas: my nightstand · the sink · my bag · the corner of my desk
fill: Today I tidied:
motto: A shadow doesn't move fast. But it never goes backwards.
Four days: you're past the halfway mark.

intro: Your legs love regularity too. Five minutes is enough to say hello to them.
task: I walk for 5 minutes
outside if possible, otherwise around the house.
Walk
ideas: walk around the block · go get bread · walk while on the phone
fill: Where I walked:
motto: The sun crosses the sky without rushing. One step after another.
Five days: your body is starting to recognize the rhythm.

intro: Tonight you give a small gift to the person you'll be tomorrow morning: you.
task: I prepare one thing for tomorrow
tonight, before bed: just one thing.
Prepare
ideas: my clothes · my bag · my glass of water on the table · my shopping list
fill: What I prepared for tomorrow:
motto: The ancients knew where tomorrow's shadow would fall. Preparing is already moving forward.
Six days: tomorrow you finish your first week.

intro: Last day of the Basic week. Today you choose the habit that did you the most good.
task: I repeat my favorite task of the week
the one that did you the most good.
Repeat
ideas: make my bed · open the window · tidy one thing · walk · prepare for tomorrow
fill: My favorite task of the week:
motto: Seven sunrises. Seven little shadows. A whole week.
Well done: turn the page for your reflection break.

intro: New step, same feet. Today we just add a little movement.
task: I stretch for 5 minutes when I wake up
gently, like a cat getting up from a nap.
Stretch
ideas: arms up to the sky · roll my shoulders · touch my toes · turn my head slowly
fill: The part of my body that said thank you:
motto: At dawn, the sundial's shadow stretches out full length on the ground. Do the same.
Eight days: a new step begins, and you're already on it.

intro: An empty surface is a little room to breathe. Today you clear one.
task: I clear one surface
10 minutes, timer on, and I keep only what matters on it.
Clear
ideas: the kitchen table · the counter · the desk · the windowsill
fill: What I found under the clutter:
motto: A sundial owns almost nothing: a stone, a stick, the light. And it works.
Nine days: around you too, something is starting to breathe.

intro: Today, a very old appointment: you, the sun, and your shadow.
task: I go outside to find my shadow
2 minutes outside: I look where it falls and note the time.
Shadow
ideas: measure it in steps · take a photo of it · raise an arm and watch it copy me
fill: Today my shadow looked like:
motto: Your shadow has followed you since your first step. It has never missed a single sunny day.
Ten days: you're in double digits.

intro: A small message can brighten a whole day. Theirs, and yours.
task: I check in on someone
a short message, just to say I'm thinking of them.
Hello
ideas: an old friend · a parent · a nice coworker · a neighbor
fill: Who I wrote to, and why them:
motto: The sun shines on everyone without choosing. One ray is enough to warm someone.
Eleven days: your light is starting to reach others.

intro: Today we don't eat more. We eat more slowly.
task: I truly savor a piece of fruit
slowly, no screen, tasting every bite.
Savor
ideas: an apple, bitten very slowly · a few cherry tomatoes · a clementine peeled in one piece
fill: Three words to describe that taste:
motto: The sundial doesn't chase noon. It waits, and noon comes to it.
Twelve days: you take your time, and time gives it back.

intro: Your phone deserves a rest too. You even more.
task: I leave my phone in another room
20 minutes, out of sight, out of reach.
Leave
ideas: during a meal · during coffee · during a slightly longer shower
fill: What I noticed without my phone:
motto: The sundial has never needed a battery. The sky is enough.
Thirteen days: tomorrow you finish the Medium step.

intro: Two habits in a row is the start of a routine. Today you make a duo.
task: I link two habits from this week
I pick two and do them one after the other, no break.
Link
ideas: stretch, then clear a surface · find my shadow, then send a hello · savor fruit, then leave my phone
fill: My duo today, and how it went:
motto: Fourteen shadows on the ground. Laid end to end, they begin to draw a circle.
Two weeks: well done, a reflection break is waiting.

intro: Welcome to the Intense step. Your day takes shape: a morning, an afternoon, an evening.
task: I give my day a shape
I write one small habit for the morning, one for the afternoon, one for the evening. And I do them.
Shape
ideas: morning: 5 minutes of stretching · afternoon: a few steps outside · evening: prepare tomorrow
fill: The moment of the day I liked best:
motto: The sundial cuts the day into hours. You cut it into three lovely pieces.
Fifteen days: your day now has a shape.

intro: Today your heart beats a little harder. Just a little, just to make it happy.
task: I walk 20 minutes, 2 of them faster
a little walking sprint in the middle, then back to my pace.
Faster
ideas: one more street than usual · take the stairs · walk to fast music
fill: When I sped up, I felt:
motto: At noon the shadow is shortest: that's when the sun gives everything.
Sixteen days: your breathing is finding its rhythm too.

intro: There's something you've been putting off for a while. Today you look it in the eye.
task: I start the task I keep putting off
just 15 minutes. Not finishing it: just starting.
Dare
ideas: an email waiting · an appointment to book · a form to fill in · a call to make
fill: What I finally started, and how it felt:
motto: A shadow you look straight at becomes tiny. Like at noon.
Seventeen days: you dare, and that's new.

intro: Evenings deserve a routine too. Tonight your screens go to bed before you.
task: I spend my last hour without screens
one hour before sleep, phone and TV off.
Unplug
ideas: read a few pages · herbal tea by the window · tidy to soft music · talk with someone
fill: What I did with that hour I got back:
motto: When the sun sets, the sundial rests. It knows the light will come back tomorrow.
Eighteen days: your evenings are learning the rhythm too.

intro: No need to be an artist. Today you just let your hand do its thing.
task: I create something for 10 minutes
draw, write, doodle: no judging, no erasing.
Create
ideas: draw my mug · write five lines about a memory · doodle to music
fill: If my creation had a title, it would be:
motto: The very first sundial was a simple line in the sand. Everything starts with a line.
Nineteen days: you're leaving a mark.

intro: A thank you said out loud changes two days at once.
task: I thank three people
out loud, looking at them, for a real reason.
Thanks
ideas: the baker · a coworker · someone at home · the bus driver
fill: The thank you that got the biggest smile:
motto: The sun gives its light every day without asking anything back. Give a little of it back.
Twenty days: tomorrow you wrap up the blue chapter.

intro: Last blue day. Today you live a whole day, from first light to last.
task: I live a complete day
one habit in the morning, one in the afternoon, one in the evening, picked from my 21 days.
Whole
ideas: morning: bed made and stretching · afternoon: a walk or a hello · evening: an hour without screens
fill: My blue chapter in one image:
motto: Twenty-one sunrises. The sundial has traced your first full circle.
Blue chapter complete. A break, then green is waiting.

intro: New chapter, new color. Green is the color of things that grow at their own pace.
task: I draw my 14 boxes
14 little squares on paper, stuck where I'll see them. I tick today's.
Box
ideas: on a sticky note · on the back of an envelope · on the fridge · in my notebook
fill: Where I put up my 14 boxes:
motto: A calendar is just boxes. What matters is what you put inside.
Twenty-two days: a fresh green page opens in front of you.

intro: Your legs carry you all day long. Today you give them back a little strength.
task: I stand up and sit down 10 times
on a chair, slowly, without my hands if I can.
Stand
ideas: while the kettle boils · after a call · in front of the window
fill: What my legs would say if they could talk:
motto: The days of a calendar stand on top of one another. Each one holds up the next.
Twenty-three days: strength is built box by box too.

intro: We often keep things for no reason. Today, five of them leave.
task: I let go of 5 things
throw out, recycle or give away. Five, not one more.
Lighten
ideas: a pen that no longer writes · clothes never worn · an old receipt · an empty box
fill: The hardest thing to let go of:
motto: Every month, the calendar turns its page. It doesn't keep the old ones on top.
Twenty-four days: you're making room for what comes next.

intro: Nature is there, even in the city. You just have to lean in a little.
task: I look at a plant up close
one minute, as if I were seeing it for the very first time.
Leaf
ideas: the veins of a leaf · the bark of a tree · a weed between two paving stones
fill: A detail I had never noticed:
motto: The very first calendars were trees: buds, flowers, fruit, then falling leaves.
Twenty-five days: you're following the rhythm of the seasons.

intro: When everything moves too fast, your breath can be your brake. Today you learn to use it.
task: I do box breathing
breathe in for 4, hold for 4, breathe out for 4, wait for 4. Four rounds.
Exhale
ideas: before a meeting · on public transport · before sleep
fill: The color of my calm today:
motto: The calendar breathes too: a day, a night, a day, a night.
Twenty-six days: your breath has found its own calendar.

intro: Really listening to someone is rare. It's a gift you can give today.
task: I ask someone a real question
and I listen to the whole answer, without preparing mine.
Listen
ideas: “What made you laugh this week?” · “What did you dream of doing as a kid?” · “What's your favorite memory?”
fill: What I learned about this person:
motto: On a calendar there are birthdays. They are always the most precious boxes.
Twenty-seven days: other people are part of your days too.

intro: Little joys hide well. Today you play at finding them.
task: I go hunting for little joys
three small beautiful things in my day, even tiny ones.
Seek
ideas: sunlight on the wall · a hot coffee · a smile in the street · a song on the radio
fill: My smallest joy today:
motto: A calendar box looks empty. Until you look a little closer.
Twenty-eight days: four weeks of coming back, almost a full turn of the moon.

intro: Your phone buzzes for lots of things that don't matter. Today we turn down the volume.
task: I turn off 3 notifications
or I delete 3 apps I never open.
Silence
ideas: alerts from a game · promos from a store · an app forgotten for months
fill: What I silenced, and what it changes:
motto: A calendar never rings. It waits quietly for you to look at it.
Twenty-nine days: less noise, more you.

intro: Habits love familiar paths. Today you surprise them a little.
task: I take a different route
to go somewhere or to come home: another street, the other sidewalk.
Detour
ideas: another street home · another bench in the park · another bakery
fill: What I discovered on this new route:
motto: Even on a tidy calendar, every box can hide a new path.
Thirty days: a whole month of coming back. The calendar can turn its page.

intro: Nobody is grading you today. It's the perfect moment to dance.
task: I dance to a whole song
alone or not, well or not, from start to finish.
Dance
ideas: in the kitchen · in the living room with headphones · with a child · in the shower
fill: The song I chose:
motto: The calendar has its holidays. Today is one, if you decide so.
Thirty-one days: even the longest months stop at 31. You keep going.

intro: Tomorrow will feel lighter if you prepare it a little tonight. Three lines are enough.
task: I write 3 things to do tomorrow
not four, not ten: three. Short and doable.
Three
ideas: one for me · one for the home · one for someone else
fill: The one I can't wait to tick off:
motto: Deep down, a calendar is a promise made to tomorrow.
Thirty-two days: you're starting to look a little further ahead.

intro: Today the task is to do nothing. It's harder than it sounds.
task: I give myself 10 minutes of nothing
no task, no screen, no goal. Just being there.
Nothing
ideas: lying on the floor · sitting in the sun · a warm cup in my hands
fill: What I thought about during that nothing:
motto: There are empty boxes on the calendar. They're part of the month too.
Thirty-three days: resting is also a way of coming back.

intro: A kind note left in the right place can travel very far.
task: I leave a small kind note
somewhere someone will find it.
Note
ideas: a sticky note on a mirror · a note slipped into a book · a message to a coworker
fill: What I wrote on my little note:
motto: On some calendars, every day has its little saying. Today you're the one writing it.
Thirty-four days: tomorrow you finish your green Basic step.

intro: Two weeks of written lines. Today you become your own reader.
task: I reread my last 14 lines
in the Journal, and I pick the one that feels most like me.
Reread
ideas: the one that makes me smile · the one that surprises me · the one I'd like to live again
fill: The line from these two weeks that I keep:
motto: Fourteen boxes ticked. The calendar is starting to tell your story.
Thirty-five days: well done, the reflection break is waiting.

intro: The green Medium step begins. A little more effort, and a little more fun.
task: I go on a 20-minute green walk
counting everything green along the way.
Green
ideas: leaves · a door · a car · a sign · a sweater
fill: My green score, and my favorite find:
motto: The green chapter lives up to its name: here, everything grows, gently.
Thirty-six days: a new step begins.

intro: No shopping, no recipe. Today your fridge throws you a challenge.
task: I cook with what I already have
a simple dish, using only the fridge and the cupboards.
Cook
ideas: an omelet · lemon pasta · leftover soup · an improvised salad
fill: The name I give my recipe:
motto: The farmers' calendar told them when to sow and when to harvest. Today, you harvest.
Thirty-seven days: you're feeding yourself, in every sense.

intro: Every home has its mystery drawer. Today you open yours.
task: I sort out a whole drawer
everything out, and only what's really useful goes back in.
Drawer
ideas: the junk drawer · the first-aid kit · the sock drawer
fill: The forgotten treasure I found:
motto: Some calendars hide a little door behind each day. A drawer is the same.
Thirty-eight days: behind every little door, a bit more space.

intro: Your brain loves new things. Today you give it a brand-new word.
task: I learn a new word and use it
in my language or another, and I put it in a sentence today.
Learn
ideas: a random word from the dictionary · a word in a foreign language · a rare, pretty word
fill: My word of the day, and the sentence I used it in:
motto: Months carry very old names: January for the god Janus, March for the god Mars. Words have a history too.
Thirty-nine days: you grow by one word.

intro: Your morning belongs to you. Today you keep it all to yourself.
task: I spend my morning without social media
until noon, I don't open it.
Free
ideas: move the app off my home screen · a book by the bed · the radio instead
fill: What I did with my morning:
motto: Before screens, people looked at the calendar on the wall. Once a day, and that was enough.
Forty days: you're taking your mornings back.

intro: A message is read. A voice is felt. Today we call.
task: I call someone instead of texting
ten minutes, a real conversation, a real voice.
Call
ideas: a grandparent · a faraway friend · a brother or sister · a former coworker
fill: The moment in the call that did me good:
motto: A voice on the phone is a calendar box filling up with warmth.
Forty-one days: bonds grow day after day too.

intro: Seven moves, seven minutes. Your body will love this little game.
task: I do 7 minutes of strength
7 moves, 1 minute each, at my own level.
Strong
ideas: squats · wall push-ups · plank on my knees · high knees · lunges
fill: The move I'd do again tomorrow, just for fun:
motto: Since the Babylonians, the week has had 7 days. Today, one minute for each of them.
Forty-two days: six weeks. Your body knows it.

intro: The sun rises and sets every day, whether we watch or not. Today you watch.
task: I watch a sunrise or a sunset
from start to finish, without taking a photo.
Light
ideas: at the window · on a balcony · at the end of the street · in a park
fill: The colors I saw:
motto: The calendar has followed the sun's path for thousands of years. Tonight, follow it too.
Forty-three days: the world keeps its appointments, and so do you.

intro: Today you become a photographer of a single color.
task: I take 5 photos of one color
I pick a color in the morning and hunt for it all day.
Color
ideas: all yellow · all red · all blue
fill: The color I chose, and why:
motto: Every month has its color: January white, April green, October gold.
Forty-four days: your day has its colors.

intro: A planner isn't only for obligations. Today you write a joy in it.
task: I schedule a joy in my calendar
a small pleasure, with a date and a time, like a real appointment.
Joy
ideas: a picnic on Sunday · a movie on Thursday night · coffee with someone · an hour of reading in bed
fill: My scheduled joy, and its date:
motto: A calendar isn't only for what you have to do. It's also for looking forward to beautiful things.
Forty-five days: halfway to 90. Take a second to feel it.

intro: Your head is full of little things buzzing around. Today you put them down on paper.
task: I empty my head for 10 minutes
I write down everything weighing on me, in no order, without sorting.
Empty
ideas: things to do · little worries · ideas lying around
fill: My head before and after, in two words:
motto: A full calendar can still feel light, if everything has its box.
Forty-six days: a tidy head, a clearer day.

intro: Helping out without being asked is a little everyday magic.
task: I do a surprise favor
something useful for someone, without waiting for thanks.
Help
ideas: carry groceries · take out a neighbor's trash · do someone's dishes · let someone go first
fill: How it felt to help:
motto: Public holidays are gifts from the calendar. You can give a small one too.
Forty-seven days: your consistency does good all around you.

intro: Even after 47 days, there are things you've never done. Today, just one.
task: I do something for the first time
small, but truly new for me.
First
ideas: taste an unknown fruit · write with my other hand · listen to music I've never heard · walk into a shop I've never visited
fill: My first time today:
motto: Every January 1st, the calendar starts over. Every day can have its own little January 1st.
Forty-eight days: you're never bored along the way.

intro: End of the green Medium step. Today you go back to your favorite habit, a little better.
task: I repeat my favorite habit of these 14 days
pushing it just a tiny bit further.
Again
ideas: a longer green walk · a second drawer · one more call · one more joy in the calendar
fill: Why this habit suits me so well:
motto: Forty-nine days, seven weeks. The calendar seems to know you well.
Well done: the reflection break is waiting.

intro: The green Intense step begins. And it starts early, with a gift: time.
task: I get up 15 minutes earlier, for me
and I keep those 15 minutes for something that does me good.
Dawn
ideas: read · stretch · drink my coffee outside · write
fill: What I did with my 15 minutes:
motto: The ancients marked on their calendars the days when the sun rose earlier. Today, so do you.
Fifty days: the number suits you.

intro: Thirty minutes of movement. All out or very gently, you set the intensity.
task: I move for 30 minutes
brisk walk, bike, swim, dance: whatever, as long as I move.
Move
ideas: brisk walking · cycling · swimming · an online class
fill: My energy afterwards, in one word:
motto: The calendar never goes back a box. Your body doesn't forget what you give it either.
Fifty-one days: you're moving forward, for real.

intro: Four hours without your phone. Scary? That's exactly what makes it interesting.
task: I spend half a day without my phone
4 hours, switched off or put away in a drawer.
Disconnect
ideas: let my loved ones know · a watch instead · something to do outside
fill: The moment I wanted to grab it, and what I did instead:
motto: For centuries, calendars were made of paper. Time passed just fine.
Fifty-two days: you're taking your time back.

intro: There's a little task lying around somewhere. Today it disappears.
task: I settle one pending matter
paperwork, appointment, repair: I finish it today.
Settle
ideas: a medical appointment · a repair · an online form · a refund
fill: The relief of being done, in one image:
motto: A crossed-out box on the calendar is one small weight less.
Fifty-three days: one less thing on your shoulders.

intro: The best moments are often lived together. Today you invite someone.
task: I invite someone to share a moment
a meal, a walk, a coffee, a game.
Share
ideas: a simple meal · a walk · a coffee · a board game
fill: The best part of that shared moment:
motto: The calendar's holidays exist for one reason: to be together.
Fifty-four days: we're stronger together.

intro: Today the most intense exercise might be sitting still and doing nothing.
task: I meditate for 10 minutes
eyes closed, I count my breaths up to 10, then start again.
Calm
ideas: with a timer · with a guided meditation · listening to the rain
fill: Where my mind wandered, and how I brought it back:
motto: Between two calendar boxes there is always a night. Calm moves you forward too.
Fifty-five days: you're learning to pause.

intro: One room, one playlist, one hour. Today cleaning becomes a concert.
task: I make one whole room shine
one hour, one playlist, one room.
Shine
ideas: the bathroom · the kitchen · the entryway · my bedroom
fill: The song that helped me most:
motto: In spring, the calendar calls for a big clean. At your place, spring is today.
Fifty-six days: eight weeks. Your space has changed with you.

intro: Your hands know how to do lots of things your head has forgotten. Today you let them lead.
task: I make something with my hands
an object, a dish, a repair, something planted.
Craft
ideas: a drawing to give away · a new dish · fix something · plant a seed
fill: What I made, and for whom:
motto: Before they were printed, calendars were painted and carved by hand.
Fifty-seven days: your hands remember.

intro: Someone helped you once, maybe without knowing it. Today you tell them.
task: I write a thank-you letter
to someone who mattered. Then I choose whether to send it.
Letter
ideas: a former teacher · a loyal friend · a parent · someone I met only once
fill: My favorite sentence in my letter:
motto: Some dates stay engraved forever. The day someone reached out to you is one of them.
Fifty-eight days: you're looking at where you come from.

intro: Today your ceiling is the sky.
task: I spend an hour outside
walking, sitting, reading: as long as it's under the sky.
Outside
ideas: a park · a forest · a waterside · a bench in the sun
fill: The outdoor sound I take with me:
motto: The calendar follows the seasons. Today you go and see them for real.
Fifty-nine days: nature comes back every year too.

intro: Two months. Enough distance to look at next week from a little higher up.
task: I plan next week
3 priorities, a moment for me, one joy.
Plan
ideas: in a notebook · in my phone's calendar · on a sheet on the fridge
fill: My number one priority:
motto: A calendar shows the whole month at a glance. Rise a little higher, you too.
Sixty days: two months. Just like that.

intro: Twenty-four hours, one challenge. You choose which, and discover what you're capable of.
task: I take on a 24-hour challenge
I pick a challenge and keep it until the same time tomorrow.
Challenge
ideas: no added sugar · not one complaint · no purchases · only water to drink
fill: My challenge, and the hardest moment:
motto: February 29th comes only once every four years. Rare days have a special taste.
Sixty-one days: you're discovering you can.

intro: Saying no to one thing means saying yes to another. Often, to yourself.
task: I say no to something, kindly
without justifying myself for ten minutes. A simple, gentle no.
No
ideas: one request too many · an evening that drains me · a task that isn't mine
fill: What my no said yes to:
motto: An overfull calendar has no room left for you. Keep a few boxes free.
Sixty-two days: protecting your time is also coming back to yourself.

intro: Last green day. Today you harvest everything you've sown in 42 days.
task: I live a complete green day
morning, afternoon, evening: one green habit in each, picked from my 42 days.
Harvest
ideas: morning: 15 minutes of dawn · afternoon: a green walk · evening: a scheduled joy
fill: What the green chapter grew in me:
motto: In 1582, ten days were removed from the calendar at once. The world went on. A missed day erases nothing.
Green chapter complete: forty-two more days. Well done.

intro: Welcome to the orange chapter. Here your habits become gears that turn one another.
task: I attach a new habit to an old one
“After this, I do that”: a tiny habit hooked onto one I already do.
Gear
ideas: after coffee, 5 squats · after brushing my teeth, one gratitude · when I get home, 2 minutes of tidying
fill: My gear of the day, “after this, I do that”:
motto: In a clock, no wheel turns alone. Each one drives the next.
Sixty-four days: the orange chapter begins. The gears are falling into place.

intro: Stairs are a free gym, open at all hours.
task: I climb stairs for 5 minutes
at my own pace, holding the rail if needed.
Climb
ideas: the ones in my building · the ones at work · the ones in the subway · a small hill
fill: How many steps, roughly:
motto: In old clocks, a weight comes down very slowly to turn the hands. Effort becomes motion.
Sixty-five days: every step counts.

intro: Curiosity is the oil that turns the gears in your head.
task: I listen to 20 minutes of something that teaches me
a subject I know nothing about.
Discover
ideas: a history podcast · a talk · a documentary · an audiobook
fill: The most surprising thing I learned:
motto: The first mechanical clocks were built by curious monks, more than 700 years ago.
Sixty-six days: your mind has its own gears.

intro: Everyone needs a place of their own, even a tiny one. Today you create yours.
task: I create my little refuge corner
a chair, a light, a beloved object: my one-square-meter refuge.
Corner
ideas: an armchair by the window · a cushion and a candle · a plant and a book
fill: The name I give my corner:
motto: In old houses, the clock had its place, and the whole room was arranged around it.
Sixty-seven days: you're making room for yourself.

intro: Your phone is a tool. Today you tidy it so it serves you, not the other way around.
task: I declutter my phone
15 minutes: home screen, photos, apps.
Sort
ideas: delete 20 blurry photos · a calming wallpaper · only useful apps on the home screen
fill: What my home screen says about me now:
motto: A well-tuned clock makes no useless noise. Just its tick-tock.
Sixty-eight days: less screen, more time.

intro: A vague compliment is forgotten. A precise one is kept for years.
task: I give a precise compliment
not a “that's nice”: a real detail I noticed.
Bravo
ideas: the way they listen · an idea in a meeting · a delicious dish · their laugh
fill: The compliment I gave, word for word:
motto: A clockmaker notices the tiniest parts. They're what make everything work.
Sixty-nine days: you see what's beautiful in others.

intro: The world moves fast. Today, for one hour, you move slower than it.
task: I do everything in slow motion for an hour
eating, walking, tidying: half as fast, twice as present.
Slow
ideas: a slow meal · a slow shower · a walk in small steps · unhurried dishes
fill: What slowness made me notice:
motto: The pendulum never rushes. That's why you can trust it.
Seventy days: you've found your own tempo.

intro: Three lines, one image, one moment. Today you're a poet.
task: I write a haiku
three short lines: a season, an image, a moment.
Poem
ideas: rain on the window · my morning coffee · the sound of the city · a falling leaf
fill: My haiku of the day:
motto: Tick, tock, tick. Three sounds are enough for a clock to tell the passing of time.
Seventy-one days: you're putting words to your days.

intro: Looking at your money isn't judging yourself. It's just switching on the light.
task: I look at my spending this week
10 minutes, no judging. Just seeing.
Count
ideas: my statements · my receipts · a budget app
fill: One expense that made me truly happy:
motto: A clock counts the seconds without ever getting upset. Count with the same gentleness.
Seventy-two days: you're facing your life, calmly.

intro: Sleep is your mainspring. Tonight you wind it a little more.
task: I go to bed 30 minutes earlier
tonight I put everything down and give myself an extra half hour of sleep.
Sleep
ideas: herbal tea · a cool room · soft light · phone out of the bedroom
fill: What I'm doing to sleep well tonight:
motto: Even the finest clock stops if you forget to wind it.
Seventy-three days: you're taking care of your mechanism.

intro: Giving doesn't empty you. Strangely, it fills you up.
task: I give something
an object, a little money, or better still, a little of my time.
Give
ideas: clothes to a charity · help a neighbor · donate blood · an hour of volunteering
fill: What I gave, and what I got back:
motto: A wheel that passes on its motion doesn't lose it. It keeps the whole clock alive.
Seventy-four days: you're turning something bigger than yourself.

intro: There's a child in you who loved something. Today you pay them a visit.
task: I revisit a childhood pleasure
20 minutes of a game or activity I loved as a kid.
Play
ideas: drawing · a puzzle · riding a bike · a card game · paper planes
fill: What the child I was would have told me:
motto: Some clocks have a cuckoo that pops out just to make you smile. Let yours out.
Seventy-five days: lightness is a strength too.

intro: Today you become the good surprise in someone's day.
task: I surprise someone
small, unexpected, just for fun.
Surprise
ideas: a breakfast made for them · a flower · a sung voice message · a dessert
fill: Their face at the moment of the surprise:
motto: A clock strikes right on the hour. A surprise strikes when you least expect it.
Seventy-six days: you're putting joy into the machinery.

intro: End of the orange Medium step. Today you choose the gears that turn best together.
task: I choose my 3 gears
out of all my habits, the 3 that fit best together, and I do them today.
Choose
ideas: one for the body · one for the mind · one for others
fill: My 3 gears:
motto: A well-tuned clock can run for centuries. So can your three gears.
Seventy-seven days: well done, the reflection break is waiting.

intro: Last step: More complex. You're no longer just following the notebook, you're starting to design your own days.
task: I draw my ideal day, hour by hour
from waking up to bedtime. Then I live at least one hour of it today.
Ideal
ideas: wake-up time · time for me · time for others · bedtime
fill: The ideal hour I lived today:
motto: A clockmaker draws every part before making it. Your day deserves a plan.
Seventy-eight days: the last step begins. You're ready.

intro: Three moves linked like gears. Today is your complete body routine.
task: I do my 20-minute body routine
5 minutes of stretching, 10 of brisk walking, 5 of strength.
Body
ideas: stretching · brisk walking · squats · plank
fill: The part of my routine I liked most:
motto: Spring, wheel, pendulum: three parts, one motion.
Seventy-nine days: your body is becoming a beautiful mechanism.

intro: Some bonds have worn a little. Today you just open the door a crack, no forcing.
task: I take a step toward a worn bond
a message to someone I've drifted from, if it's good for me.
Mend
ideas: “I'm thinking of you” · a simple apology · a shared memory
fill: What I dared to write:
motto: A stopped clock can always start again. All it takes is a patient clockmaker.
Eighty days: you have a big heart.

intro: In a year, you'll be a year further along anyway. Might as well arrive with something new.
task: I take my first lesson
20 minutes on a skill I want to have in a year.
Begin
ideas: a language · an instrument · coding · sewing · a dish from elsewhere
fill: In a year, I'll know how to:
motto: It took centuries to invent an accurate clock. One lesson a day is already a lot.
Eighty-one days: you're planting for later.

intro: A whole day without social media. The world will turn without you, and you'll turn better.
task: I spend a whole day without social media
24 hours, apps hidden or deleted for the day.
Offline
ideas: let my loved ones know · a notebook for what I wanted to share · an outing planned
fill: What I would have posted, and what I lived instead:
motto: Long ago, the church tower clock told the time to a whole village. It was enough to live together.
Eighty-two days: you're taking back a whole day.

intro: You've already sorted a drawer, then a room. Today you sort a whole category.
task: I pare down a whole category
all my clothes, or all my books, or all my cables: I keep what I truly love.
Pare
ideas: clothes · books · papers · cables
fill: What I'm keeping, and why I love it:
motto: A clock has no spare parts. Every wheel has its reason to be there.
Eighty-three days: you keep what's essential.

intro: Twelve weeks on the road. Time to put what you've learned into a single sentence.
task: I write my motto
a short sentence to guide me, to keep with me.
Motto
ideas: “Always come back” · “Small, but every day” · “Slowly, but surely”
fill: My motto:
motto: On some old clocks, people engraved a motto. Yours deserves to be engraved too.
Eighty-four days: twelve weeks. You know who you're becoming.

intro: There's a project that has waited a long time for you. Today you give it a whole hour.
task: I give an hour to a project close to my heart
one uninterrupted hour, phone away, door closed.
Project
ideas: writing · a garden · a photo album · a trip to plan · a website
fill: My project in one sentence, like a promise:
motto: Some clockmakers spent their entire life on a single clock. Great things love patience.
Eighty-five days: only five to go. Your own mechanism runs by itself.

intro: You've done much more than you think. Today you prove it in black and white.
task: I write down 20 things I've achieved
since day 1, or ever. Small ones count double.
Proud
ideas: a sorted drawer · a call made · a morning without my phone · coming back after a missed day
fill: The achievement I'm proudest of:
motto: Every tick-tock is a small victory over time. You've collected millions of them.
Eighty-six days: look at everything you've done.

intro: A shared habit holds twice as well. Today you bring someone along.
task: I bring someone along with me
I invite someone to do one habit together every day for a week.
Together
ideas: walk together · send each other a gratitude every evening · cook together on Sundays
fill: Who I'm bringing along, and our habit:
motto: In 1665, Huygens noticed that two clocks hung side by side ended up ticking together.
Eighty-seven days: your consistency is becoming contagious.

intro: Day 90 isn't an ending. Today you prepare what comes next.
task: I prepare my 30 days after
which habits I keep, when I do them, and what will remind me.
After
ideas: 3 habits every day · 1 big habit a week · a reminder on my phone · a calendar on the fridge
fill: The habit I'm keeping forever:
motto: A clock doesn't stop at midnight. It simply starts a new round.
Eighty-eight days: you're already looking further ahead.

intro: Second to last day. Today you travel your whole path in a single day.
task: I live a day of my whole path
a blue habit, a green habit, an orange habit: from simplest to most complex.
All
ideas: blue: find my shadow · green: a scheduled joy · orange: a slow hour
fill: The habit that has changed most since the beginning:
motto: A clock doesn't show all its wheels. But each one worked to get here.
Eighty-nine days: tomorrow, the last one.

intro: Day 90. Today you go back to where it all began, to see the whole path.
task: I redo my day 1
the same small habits, and I reread my very first line.
Return
ideas: the same glass of water · the same small task · reread my first line in the Journal
fill: What I'd tell the me of day 1:
motto: The shadow, the pages, the gears: everything led you here.
Ninety days. You came back, again and again. Purple is waiting.
